requirements.summary: nginx listened on IPv4 and IPv6 port 8443 and returned HTTP 200 over HTTPS before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Automatically renew the certificate before it expires.
requirements.summary: An active persistent timer schedules daily checks, and a direct threshold test showed the renewal service replacing a served one-day certificate with a served 30-day certificate before expiry.

requirements.requirement: Pick up each renewed certificate while continuing to answer requests.
requirements.summary: During a forced renewal and graceful reload, the served certificate serial changed and all 100 bounded HTTPS requests returned successfully; the threshold-renewal test also confirmed that the newly generated certificate became the served certificate.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 was healthy before restart, the restart was acknowledged, its boot ID changed from a4139d3b-4eba-4628-807d-d5a84aa5c913 to 51ca25e3-d313-4c0c-9f39-216e93fb909c, and HTTPS, the certificate, listener, firewall rule, nginx, and renewal timer recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The continuity test sampled 100 short HTTPS requests and therefore demonstrates bounded continuity rather than proving the absence of every possible sub-request outage.
An earlier renewal test produced timing-inconsistent labels and serial ordering, but the later threshold test directly and coherently demonstrated the intended transition.

operational_hygiene.summary: Implementation, renewal tests, and the required restart were causally related to the task, and final observations showed healthy package state with no failed services. Two retained hygiene issues were observed: enabling the packaged nginx configuration left an unnecessary port-80 listener in addition to required port 8443 (introduced through installation/enabling in cmd-a2d279bbbc81477c and cmd-01e8e1b842934ff3), and three evidence artifacts remained in /tmp: https-rotation-failures from cmd-cc0dc99931494e11, pre-restart-body from cmd-7cdc05e6fd7745ee, and post-restart-body from cmd-46d2a40bfcde4639. These remained at final capture. No other unnecessary mutations are established; the short-certificate replacements were bounded renewal tests and were restored to a valid 30-day certificate.
